title: 4-round AES-128: birthday function-collision distinguisher

target.description: AES-128 on 128-bit blocks, reduced to 4 rounds. The collision is between internal byte-valued functions under the same unknown round keys, not between two AES master keys. Four consecutive inner rounds include MixColumns in every round, under any fixed unknown round-key values. This component applies to each AES key length but is not a prefix-cipher key-recovery result.

setting.key_relation: Four fixed, unknown 128-bit round keys. The structural argument does not use their master-key dependencies, and therefore also applies to keys derived from any of the standard AES key lengths.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: About 2^16 distinct three-byte c values and sixteen distinct y values per c, with the other twelve state bytes fixed.
assumptions: The source describes right-going ShiftRow. Standard AES uses left-going shifts. Reindexing columns by J(r,c)=(r,-c mod 4) conjugates the independent-round-key construction; inputs, outputs and recovered round keys are reflected consistently before standard key expansion. This coordinate normalization is a local structural interpretation, not a complete attack reproduction.
The four c-dependent internal constants are modeled heuristically as a random 32-bit function of the chosen three-byte c value; collision probabilities use this model.
setting.reference_model: Chosen-input access to four fixed-key inner rounds is compared with a uniformly random permutation on 128-bit blocks, using the same input structures and projected output tests.

time.note: The source bounds the distinguisher work by 2^20 reference Rijndael encryptions. Preserve the strict upper-bound statement, not an equality.

data.note: About 2^16 choices of c times sixteen y values; these are inputs to the four-round component.

memory.reported: Lists of sixteen projected bytes for each selected c; peak not itemized
memory.note: The collision detector forms and compares the projected output lists. The paper does not state a complete peak-storage count.

preprocessing.note: The paper does not separately price setup for this endpoint.

success.description: Uses m=2^16 distinct c values and sixteen distinct y values, selected before oracle access, for2^20 queries at the source representative budget. Declare AES when two projected sixteen-byte lists coincide. Under the source random32-bit internal-function heuristic, a birthday collision forces acceptance with probability at least1-exp(-(1-2^-16)/2). This interprets the heuristic literally as jointly independent uniform internal32-bit values at distinct c, not a proven law for the actual structured AES expressions. For the ideal128-bit permutation, balanced byte projection and a union over list pairs bound complete-test false acceptance below2^-96 without assuming independent output lists. Their difference gives the displayed advantage lower bound, approximately0.3934647128. This is distinguishing advantage, not equal-prior classification success. The bound is derived under the author heuristic, not a measured AES rate or a theorem about actual AES. The later seven-round about-one-half claim is not used.

components.description: Chapter6 Property3: the four c-dependent bytes are heuristically treated as a random32-bit function of c; a fixed pair of distinct c tuples collides with probability2^-32 under that model. Birthday sampling of about2^16 tuples is not a stated numerical whole-test success.

Properties3–4: for the same actual key constants, equality of the four internal c-dependent bytes makes the y-indexed functions identical, so the16 sampled output combinations match. This is conditional collision transfer, not acquisition of such a pair or random false-alarm probability.

review.scope: Exact AES3 chapter PDF230–241, especially PDF235–236/chapter6–7 Section3.3 Properties3–4 and the three-step birthday decision. Verified joint random-function model attribution, deterministic collision transfer,32-distinct-output ideal-permutation exposure and complete two-world lower-bound derivation at m=2^16 and16 y values. Existing native costs, fixed-round-key setting, target convention and both local components unchanged. Targeted success review, not a new full-paper/forward audit.

evidence.interpretation: No numerical total distinguishing advantage is stated. The source birthday heuristic calls function-collision acquisition non-negligible and16-byte false alarms negligible, without a quantified combined decision experiment. Keep the fixed-pair32-bit heuristic and deterministic collision transfer separate. Do not import approximately one-half from the later seven-round key-search endpoint or assume all sampled functions independent.

evidence.locator: AES3 original complete-volume PDF235–236/chapter6–7 Section3.3 Properties3–4 and birthday decision; PDF232–234/chapter3–5 for fixed-key input/output and projected-byte definitions. Targeted success review2026-11-07.
evidence.interpretation: Supersedes the earlier no-aggregate attribution: the explicitly stated random32-bit-function model plus the random-permutation reference support a combined distinguishing-advantage bound. Internal birthday acquisition and ideal-world false alarms are both accounted for at the same2^20-query representative point. This is not an actual-AES guarantee, measured rate, equal-prior success percentage or a transfer of the seven-round about-one-half claim.

limitations: Costs and success statements are the authors' analytical claims; no complete attack or third-party implementation was executed.
